s: Today we are talking about getting around, buses, trains, cars, and travel.
Every day, millions of people use public transit.
Transit is the system of buses, trains, and subways in a city.
A good transit system changes everything.
In my city, the transit is clean and fast.
I take the transit to work every single morning.
When the transit is on time, my day starts well.
Cities with great transit feel alive.
Do you know who uses the transit most?
A commuter is a person who travels to work or school every day.
A smart commuter leaves home early.
I was a commuter for five years, and every commuter learns the best seat on the train.
A tired commuter just wants a quiet ride.
Every commuter I know has a podcast or a book for the trip.
And every commuter needs a timetable.
A timetable is a list showing when buses or trains arrive and leave.
The timetable is my morning bible.
I check the timetable while I drink my coffee.
If the timetable changes, my whole plan changes.
Modern timetables live on our phones.
A clear timetable means no long waits in the rain.
I always save the timetable for the way home too.
The fare is the money you pay to travel by bus, train, or taxi.
Fares go up, fares go down.
The bus fare here is two dollars.
A monthly card is cheaper than paying the fare every day.
Students pay a lower fare in many cities.
If the fare is fair, more people ride.
A high fare pushes people back into cars.
On the train, you meet the conductor.
A conductor is a person who checks tickets on a train or bus.
When the conductor comes, everyone shows a ticket.
A friendly conductor makes the trip better.
The conductor knows all the regulars.
A good conductor helps lost tourists too.
I once saw a conductor return a lost bag to its owner.
At the station, you take the escalator.
An escalator is moving stairs that carry people up or down.
The escalator at the main station is so long.
Stand on the right of the escalator, walk on the left.
Kids ride the escalator just for fun.
The new escalator near my office is made of glass.
Sometimes the road is closed, and you need a detour.
A detour is a longer road you take when the usual road is closed.
Last week a detour added twenty minutes to my trip.
But a detour can also show you a pretty street.
My driver took a clever detour yesterday and beat the traffic.
A bad detour wastes your morning.
Always ask why there is a detour.
In the city, every road meets at an intersection.
An intersection is a place where two or more roads meet.
At every intersection, watch the lights.
The intersection by my office has the longest red light ever.
Be extra careful at a big intersection.
Cars, bikes, and people share the intersection.
I always look both ways at an intersection.
For longer trips, take the highway.
A highway is a wide, fast road between cities.
The highway to the beach takes two hours.
Early on a Sunday, the highway is completely empty.
A highway at rush hour is a different story.
Every highway has rest stops for coffee.
We sang songs all the way down the highway.
And for travel abroad, you need a passport.
A passport is a small official book you need to travel to other countries.
My passport is full of stamps.
I keep my passport in a special pocket.
Check that your passport is valid before you book a flight.
Without a passport, no international trip.
Every traveler should know where their passport is.
Before we finish, let's share our best travel tips.
Lena, what is your number one rule for the transit?
Always check the timetable first, and keep some coins for the fare.
If the fare machine is broken, coins save the day.
A prepared commuter never gets stuck.
Take the escalator when you have luggage, but learn where it ends.
And smile at the conductor, because a happy conductor remembers you.
My tip for drivers is this.
When there is a detour, stay calm and follow the signs.
And at every intersection, slow down, even if the light is green.
My last tip is for road trips.
Plan your highway stops before you leave.
A good highway plan means good coffee.
And always check your passport the night before a flight, not at the airport.
I learned that the hard way.
If you are a new commuter in a new city, ride the transit for fun on the weekend.
Learn the lines, learn the fare system, and you will feel at home fast.
Travel is easier when you know the words.
Let's say them together one more time, nice and slow.
A detour saves you when roads close.
The intersection is where roads meet.
Describe your transit, or tell a friend about a funny detour.
Thanks for listening to Word Kitchen.
